proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(L\ge2\), a compatible marginal vector \(p\), and \(d\in\mathcal D\).  At the optimization level of this theorem the input is the full marginal vector \(p=(p_{rj})_{r,j}\).  If \(p\) is obtained from an observed randomized law, the observable map is \(P\mapsto(P(Y=j\mid A=r))_{r,j}\); the theorem itself uses only the supplied value of \(p\) and the maintained support \(\mathcal U_L\).  To keep the causal object distinct from its observed-law bound, define the scalar identified set induced by these marginals and the support restriction as
\[
 \Theta_{I,d}(p)=\{\theta_d(q):q\in\Gamma_L(p)\}.
\]
By \(\text{def:coupling-fiber}\), compatibility is exactly feasibility of
\[
 G_Lq=p,\qquad q\ge0.
 \tag{1}
\]
Summing the \(L\) equations for any fixed arm in (1) gives \(\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}q(u)=1\).  Hence \(\Gamma_L(p)\) is a closed subset of the finite probability simplex and is compact.  It is convex, and \(q\mapsto\theta_d(q)\) is linear by \(\text{def:unique-peak-indicators}\).  Therefore \(\Theta_{I,d}(p)\) is the compact interval
\[
 \Theta_{I,d}(p)=[\underline\theta_d(p),\overline\theta_d(p)].
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus any equality proved below is a sharp endpoint characterization, not merely an outer bound.

Put \(c^{(d)}_u=B_d(u)\).  The lower endpoint is the finite linear program
\[
 \min_{q\ge0}\left\{(c^{(d)})^{\mathsf T}q:G_Lq=p\right\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
It has an optimizer by compactness.  Its equality-form dual is
\[
 \max_{y\in\mathbb R^{3L}}
 \left\{p^{\mathsf T}y:G_L^{\mathsf T}y\le c^{(d)}\right\};
 \tag{4}
\]
the dual variable is unrestricted in sign because the primal constraints are equalities.  Applying the finite linear-programming strong-duality result \(\text{lem:finite-lp-strong-duality}\), in the exact form attributed there to Trevisan, Lecture 6, Theorem 6.5, shows that (4) attains the value of (3).  Since
\[
 (G_L^{\mathsf T}y)_u=\sum_{r\in\mathcal D}y_{r,u_r},
 \qquad
 p^{\mathsf T}y=\sum_{r\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y_L}p_{rj}y_{rj},
\]
this is the asserted lower dual formula.  Applying the same theorem to the maximization primal
\[
 \max_{q\ge0}\left\{(c^{(d)})^{\mathsf T}q:G_Lq=p\right\}
\]
gives the attained dual minimum
\[
 \min_{z\in\mathbb R^{3L}}
 \left\{p^{\mathsf T}z:G_L^{\mathsf T}z\ge c^{(d)}\right\},
\]
which is the asserted upper formula.  Combining these equalities with (2) proves that the displayed dual values equal the sharp causal endpoints over all compatible latent couplings; that relationship was derived from the coupling fiber and was not imposed by definition.

We next derive the exact separator.  For \(r\in\{0,2\}\) and \(k\in\mathcal Y_L\), define
\[
 P_r^{\le}(k)=\max_{0\le j\le k}x_{rj},\qquad
 P_r^{<}(k)=\max_{0\le j<k}x_{rj},\qquad
 S_r^{>}(k)=\max_{k<j<L}x_{rj},
 \tag{5}
\]
where a maximum over an empty set is \(-\infty\).  The recursions
\[
 P_r^{\le}(k)=\max\{P_r^{\le}(k-1),x_{rk}\},
 \qquad
 S_r^{>}(k)=\max\{x_{r,k+1},S_r^{>}(k+1)\}
\]
with the evident boundary conventions compute all quantities in (5) in one forward and one backward pass, using \(O(L)\) exact additions and comparisons.

Fix \(u_1=k\).  By \(\text{def:non-valley-support}\), legality is equivalent to \(u_0\le k\) or \(u_2\le k\).  The legal pairs \((u_0,u_2)\) form the following five disjoint regions:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{region}&\text{conditions}&B_d(u)\\ \hline
R_0&u_0>k,\ u_2\le k&\mathbf 1\{d=0\}\\
R_2&u_2>k,\ u_0\le k&\mathbf 1\{d=2\}\\
R_1&u_0<k,\ u_2<k&\mathbf 1\{d=1\}\\
R_{01}&u_0=k,\ u_2\le k&0\\
R_{12}&u_0<k,\ u_2=k&0.
\end{array}
 \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, if \(u_0>k\), legality forces \(u_2\le k\), giving \(R_0\); if \(u_2>k\), legality forces \(u_0\le k\), giving \(R_2\); otherwise both outer coordinates are at most \(k\), and the last three rows of (6) partition that case according as both inequalities are strict, only the first is an equality, or only the second is an equality.  On these regions, direct additive maximization gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 V_{0d}(k)&=S_0^{>}(k)+x_{1k}+P_2^{\le}(k)-\sigma\mathbf 1\{d=0\},\\
 V_{2d}(k)&=P_0^{\le}(k)+x_{1k}+S_2^{>}(k)-\sigma\mathbf 1\{d=2\},\\
 V_{1d}(k)&=P_0^{<}(k)+x_{1k}+P_2^{<}(k)-\sigma\mathbf 1\{d=1\},\\
 V_{01,d}(k)&=x_{0k}+x_{1k}+P_2^{\le}(k),\\
 V_{12,d}(k)&=P_0^{<}(k)+x_{1k}+x_{2k}.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \max_{u\in\mathcal U_L}
 \left\{\sum_{r\in\mathcal D}x_{r,u_r}-\sigma B_d(u)\right\}
 =\max_{k\in\mathcal Y_L}
 \max\{V_{0d}(k),V_{2d}(k),V_{1d}(k),V_{01,d}(k),V_{12,d}(k)\}.
 \tag{8}
\]
For the lower dual take \(x=y\) and \(\sigma=1\); its candidate is feasible exactly when (8) is at most zero.  For the upper dual take \(x=-z\) and \(\sigma=-1\), because the left side of (8) then equals
\[
 \max_{u\in\mathcal U_L}\left\{B_d(u)-\sum_{r\in\mathcal D}z_{r,u_r}\right\}.
\]
Keeping an argmax in every prefix and suffix recursion also returns a maximizing legal triple, and hence a violated dual constraint whenever the maximum is positive.  This proves the \(O(L)\) exact separation claim.  Because \(\mathcal U_L\) is finite, adding a newly violated constraint terminates after at most \(|\mathcal U_L|\) additions; equivalently, one may enumerate all legal columns and solve the resulting finite rational program.  Thus rational input gives a fully exact finite computation without any catalogue of canonical facets.

For completeness, we prove the stronger rational-input complexity and sparsity corollary.  A triple is excluded precisely when, for \(u_1=k\), both outer coordinates lie in \(\{k+1,\ldots,L-1\}\).  Hence
\[
 |\mathcal U_L|
 =L^3-\sum_{k=0}^{L-2}(L-1-k)^2
 =L^3-\sum_{m=1}^{L-1}m^2
 =L^3-\frac{(L-1)L(2L-1)}6
 =O(L^3).
 \tag{9}
\]
The explicit feasibility program and each of the six primal endpoint programs therefore have a number of binary-encoded rational coefficients polynomial in \(L\) and in the encoding length of \(p\).  The rational linear-programming algorithm in \(\text{lem:rational-lp-polynomial-time}\) decides compatibility and, when compatible, returns the exact optimum of every one of these six bounded programs in polynomial time.

To expose the optimizer construction and its support bound, replace the redundant full marginal equations by the matrix \(M_L\) whose rows are one normalization row and the \(3(L-1)\) rows indexed by \((r,j)\in\mathcal D\times\{1,\ldots,L-1\}\):
\[
 (M_L)_{\varnothing,u}=1,
 \qquad
 (M_L)_{(r,j),u}=\mathbf 1\{u_r=j\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
For \(b(p)=(1,(p_{rj})_{r,1\le j<L})^{\mathsf T}\), the simplex identities imply
\[
 \Gamma_L(p)=\{q\ge0:M_Lq=b(p)\}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, the omitted level-zero equation for arm \(r\) is
\[
 \sum_{u:u_r=0}q(u)
 =1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}p_{rj}=p_{r0}.
\]
The matrix in (10) has only \(3L-2\) rows.  An optimal basic feasible solution consequently has at most \(3L-2\) positive entries.  Such a solution is obtainable within the stated polynomial bound.  After computing the rational optimal value \(v\), start with the nonempty compact rational polytope obtained from (11) by adding the equality \((c^{(d)})^{\mathsf T}q=v\).  In a fixed ordering of its \(O(L^3)\) coordinates, sequentially minimize each coordinate over the face left by all preceding minimizations and add the equality fixing that coordinate at its attained minimum.  Each minimum is attained at a vertex of the original optimal face, so Cramer's rule applied to a submatrix of the original rational system bounds its encoding length polynomially in the original input.  Each step is therefore an exact rational linear program of polynomial encoding length, and there are \(O(L^3)\) steps.  At the end every coordinate is fixed, so the remaining face is a singleton.  A singleton face of the optimal face is an extreme point of (11), hence a basic optimal solution.  If the positive columns of \(M_L\) at that point were dependent, a sufficiently small two-sided null perturbation would express it as the midpoint of two distinct feasible points, contradicting extremality.  Thus its support has size at most \(\operatorname{rank}(M_L)\le3L-2\).

The same support bound also has an explicit support-elimination certificate.  If a rational optimizer \(q\) has support \(S\) with \(|S|>3L-2\), the columns \((M_{L,u})_{u\in S}\) are dependent, so exact Gaussian elimination returns nonzero rational \(a\), supported on \(S\), with \(M_La=0\).  The normalization row implies \(\sum_ua(u)=0\), so \(a\) has both signs.  For sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), both \(q+\varepsilon a\) and \(q-\varepsilon a\) are feasible.  Optimality for either the minimum or maximum of the linear cost forces
\[
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}B_d(u)a(u)=0;
\]
otherwise one of the two signs would improve the objective.  Therefore
\[
 t=\min_{u\in S:a(u)<0}\frac{q(u)}{-a(u)}>0
\]
makes \(q+ta\) a rational optimizer with strictly smaller support.  At most \(|\mathcal U_L|-(3L-2)\) repetitions give a rational endpoint optimizer supported on at most \(3L-2\) legal triples.  The preceding sequential-face construction supplies such a basic optimizer with a polynomial number of exact rational-LP calls, while this elimination argument certifies the support bound equation by equation.  Thus compatibility, all six endpoints, and sparse rational endpoint-attaining mixtures are exactly computable in time polynomial in \(L\) and the input bit length, while the all-\(L\) canonical facet stream remains unnecessary for scalar endpoint evaluation.

added_lemmas.statement: Every finite linear program with binary-encoded rational coefficients can be solved by an exact algorithm whose running time is polynomial in the total input encoding length: the algorithm decides feasibility and, when the feasible objective is bounded, returns an exact rational optimal value and an exact rational optimal solution.

source.locator: Lecture 5, Section 2.4 (Polynomial Time Algorithms for Linear Programming)

attestation.note: The cited section states polynomial-time solvability of linear programming and explains exact recovery from the polynomial-bit rational coordinates of an optimum.

added_lemmas.statement: Fix \(L\ge2\).  Given a rational vector \(p\in\prod_{d\in\mathcal D}\Delta^{L-1}\) in binary encoding, whether \(\Gamma_L(p)\) is empty is decidable in time polynomial in \(L\) and the total input bit length.  If it is nonempty, all six values \(\underline\theta_d(p)\) and \(\overline\theta_d(p)\), \(d\in\mathcal D\), are exactly computable within the same complexity class.  For each endpoint, the algorithm also constructs a rational optimizer \(q^\star\in\Gamma_L(p)\) with \(|\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)|\le3L-2\).  These conclusions use \(|\mathcal U_L|=L^3-(L-1)L(2L-1)/6=O(L^3)\) and do not require enumeration of \(\mathcal H_L\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For a fixed middle response \(u_1=k\), the illegal strict valleys have independently chosen outer coordinates \(u_0,u_2\in\{k+1,\ldots,L-1\}\), and therefore number \((L-1-k)^2\).  Summing over \(k=0,\ldots,L-2\) gives
\[
 |\mathcal U_L|
 =L^3-\sum_{k=0}^{L-2}(L-1-k)^2
 =L^3-\frac{(L-1)L(2L-1)}6.
 \tag{12}
\]
In particular, the legal-incidence matrix in \(\text{thm:direct-support-transport-dual}\) has \(3L\) rows and \(O(L^3)\) columns, all with zero--one entries.  For rational \(p\), its binary description has length polynomial in \(L\) and the input encoding length.  Apply \(\text{lem:rational-lp-polynomial-time}\) first to the feasibility system \(G_Lq=p\), \(q\ge0\).  This decides whether \(\Gamma_L(p)\) is empty.  When it is nonempty, apply the same result to the minimization and maximization programs with cost \((B_d(u))_{u\in\mathcal U_L}\), for each of the three values of \(d\).  Their feasible set is contained in the probability simplex and is therefore bounded.  The direct-support dual theorem identifies their six exact optimal values with \(\underline\theta_d(p)\) and \(\overline\theta_d(p)\).  A constant number of polynomial-time calls remains polynomial, proving the computation claim.

It remains to construct the stated optimizer.  Let \(M_L\) have the normalization row and the \(3(L-1)\) nonzero-level marginal rows,
\[
 (M_L)_{\varnothing,u}=1,
 \qquad
 (M_L)_{(r,j),u}=\mathbf 1\{u_r=j\},
 \qquad 1\le j<L.
\]
For \(b(p)=(1,(p_{rj})_{r,1\le j<L})^{\mathsf T}\), the simplex equations give
\[
 \Gamma_L(p)=\{q\ge0:M_Lq=b(p)\},
 \tag{13}
\]
because the omitted equation equals \(1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}p_{rj}=p_{r0}\) for every arm \(r\).  For a polynomial-time basic-solution construction, first compute the rational optimal value \(v\).  Add \(c^{\mathsf T}q=v\) to (13), fix an ordering of the \(O(L^3)\) coordinates, and sequentially minimize each coordinate over the nonempty compact face left by preceding minimizations, fixing that coordinate at its exact attained value after each call.  Each minimum is attained at a vertex of the original optimal face; Cramer's rule for a nonsingular submatrix of the original rational system therefore gives it encoding length polynomial in the original input.  The cited algorithm consequently solves every one of these polynomial-size rational programs in polynomial time.  After all coordinates have been fixed, the remaining face is a singleton, hence an extreme point of (13).  Its positive columns of \(M_L\) are linearly independent: otherwise a sufficiently small two-sided null perturbation would express it as the midpoint of two distinct feasible points.  Consequently this rational optimizer has support at most \(\operatorname{rank}(M_L)\le3L-2\).  The number of calls is polynomial because there are \(O(L^3)\) coordinates.

For an equation-by-equation support certificate starting from any rational optimizer \(q\), suppose its support \(S\) has more than \(3L-2\) elements.  Then the corresponding columns of the \((3L-2)\)-row matrix \(M_L\) are dependent.  Exact Gaussian elimination produces nonzero rational \(a\), supported on \(S\), with \(M_La=0\).  The normalization row makes \(a\) have both signs.  Both \(q+\varepsilon a\) and \(q-\varepsilon a\) are feasible for all sufficiently small positive \(\varepsilon\).  If \(c_u=B_d(u)\) is the endpoint cost, optimality of \(q\) under these two perturbations implies \(c^{\mathsf T}a=0\).  Thus
\[
 t=\min_{u\in S:a(u)<0}\frac{q(u)}{-a(u)}
\]
is positive and rational, and \(q+ta\) is a rational optimizer with at least one fewer positive coordinate.  Repeating yields a rational optimizer with the asserted support.  The sequential-face construction above establishes the polynomial-time guarantee without requiring a bound on the intermediate fractions along this optional elimination path.  Only the legal incidence matrix, the endpoint cost, and the observed marginal vector enter either construction, so no enumeration of \(\mathcal H_L\) is used.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(L\ge2\).  Let \(G_L\) be the \(3L\)-by-\(|\mathcal U_L|\) legal-response incidence matrix with rows indexed by \((r,j)\in\mathcal D\times\mathcal Y_L\), columns indexed by \(u\in\mathcal U_L\), and entries \((G_L)_{(r,j),u}=\mathbf 1\{u_r=j\}\).  For \(d\in\mathcal D\), let \(c^{(d)}_u=B_d(u)\), and regard \(p=(p_{rj})_{r,j}\) here as the full \(3L\)-vector of arm probabilities.  For every compatible \(p\),
\[
 \underline\theta_d(p)=
 \max_{y\in\mathbb R^{3L}}
 \left\{\sum_{r\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y_L}p_{rj}y_{rj}:
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal D}y_{r,u_r}\le B_d(u)\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U_L\right\},
\]
and
\[
 \overline\theta_d(p)=
 \min_{z\in\mathbb R^{3L}}
 \left\{\sum_{r\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y_L}p_{rj}z_{rj}:
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal D}z_{r,u_r}\ge B_d(u)\quad\forall u\in\mathcal U_L\right\}.
\]
Both dual optima are attained.  Moreover, feasibility of either dual candidate has an \(O(L)\) exact separation oracle.  For arrays \(x=(x_{rj})\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), all prefix and suffix maxima can be computed in two passes, after which
\[
 \max_{u\in\mathcal U_L}\left\{\sum_{r\in\mathcal D}x_{r,u_r}-\sigma B_d(u)\right\}
\]
is the maximum, over \(k\in\mathcal Y_L\), of five explicitly evaluable region scores corresponding to \(u_0>k,u_2\le k\); \(u_2>k,u_0\le k\); \(u_0<k,u_2<k\); \(u_0=k,u_2\le k\); and \(u_0<k,u_2=k\).  Thus scalar endpoints can be computed by a finite linear program with this separator, using exact rational arithmetic whenever \(p\) is rational.  The complete all-\(L\) canonical facet stream is needed to catalogue the joint polytope, but is not needed merely to evaluate a scalar endpoint.
proposed.justification: The direct legal-incidence program yields sharp scalar endpoints, an exact \(O(L)\) separator, polynomial-time rational compatibility and endpoint computation, and rational sparse optimizers without the unresolved facet catalogue.
proposed.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian's arbitrary-objective transport architecture can encode the support with extended costs, but its quadratic-objective rate does not transfer.  The present finite legal-support program and its exact algorithmic consequences are proved directly, using Trevisan's Theorem 6.5 for strong duality.
proposed.consumer: All six scalar endpoints and endpoint-attaining worst-case response mixtures can be computed before the all-\(L\) canonical joint-polytope stream is known.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The strengthened proof uses the standard rational linear-programming algorithmic result to establish the requested polynomial-time corollary, so that cited result must be added to the theorem's declared proof spine.

proposed.comparator_claim: Discrete causal bounds can be computed as polynomial programs with convergent anytime outer bounds.
Finite causal response-type models can have complete observable facet inequalities beyond Pearl's basic instrumental inequality.
A deterministic parent map supports duplicate-free reverse-search enumeration without storing visited objects.

Two-arm ordinal benefit probabilities have sharp cumulative formulas for unrestricted bivariate potential-outcome couplings; those formulas do not transfer sharply to the three-way non-valley support restriction.
Two-potential-outcome distributional bounds under support restrictions admit a Kantorovich-dual characterization.

Arbitrary-objective multi-marginal transport can represent the present legal-support problem after an explicit extended-cost encoding of illegal cells; the paper's quadratic-objective plug-in rate does not transfer to the unique-peak indicator, for which the present work proves an equivalent finite legal-incidence program directly.

Their compatibility graph concerns observable implications of potential-response support restrictions and requires every maximal clique to correspond to a support point.  Here every two-dose projection is full, so the graph is complete tripartite and every triple is a maximal three-clique, including the deleted strict-middle valleys; that premise fails, and the present polytope additionally augments arm marginals by three unique-peak target coordinates.
Randomly perturbed LP value functions yield uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals of set-identified parameters.
For Gaussian first-stage limits, ordinary bootstrap consistency is equivalent to full differentiability, and a derivative-estimation bootstrap handles directional maps.
Intersection bounds admit adaptive inequality selection and Gaussian-process inference.
Continuous functionals of the joint distribution of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model admit sharp bounds through random-set restrictions and convex optimization.

For binary treatment and an ordinal outcome, exact randomization inference in the paper assumes independent potential outcomes and concerns the relative treatment effect, not the present three-dose unique-best endpoint map.

Sharp symbolic ordinal bounds are derived for binary-exposure observational confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs; they do not classify or evaluate a three-dose forbidden-support unique-best polytope.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Kaido--Ponomarev comparison is expanded to state the precise failed clique premise and the distinct augmented target coordinates, while the transport comparison is synchronized with the proved direct legal-support program.

prose_updates.tldr: Randomization identifies the three marginals of a prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score but not the population shares for which each dose is uniquely best.  Under weak individual unimodality, the compatible target vectors form a structured three-marginal polytope.  The staircase family with \(3^{L-3}\) weighted facets, the exact small-support counts \(59\), \(197\), and \(721\), and sharp endpoint formulas using at most three full facets are proved.  Independently of any all-support facet stream, a finite legal-incidence program computes all six scalar endpoints exactly in polynomial time for rational input, constructs endpoint-attaining rational mixtures with support at most \(3L-2\), and the \(L=2\) equal-Bernoulli example proves that this support bound is uniformly sharp.  Fixed-\(L\) plug-in rates and exact finite-sample simultaneous endpoint coverage, including zero cells and realized empty arms, are also proved.  The remaining mathematical questions are the all-\(L\) exact-once stream with its finite predecessor and transfer classification, and regular-face equivalence of the exact scalar procedure to a specified efficient Wald interval.  The Goodwin et al. application remains an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis: the trial identifies score marginals but neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality.

project_justification.gap: Existing two-dose results sharply bound functionals of two potential outcomes, and generic discrete causal or multi-marginal optimizers can return numerical bounds.  The cited two-potential-outcome and generic optimization works do not study the paper-specific task of classifying \(\mathcal H_L\) by a finite predecessor map satisfying \(\mathsf{CHECK}_{2\mathrm{BTAS}}\).  Kaido and Ponomarev's maximal-clique correspondence does not cover this support: all two-dose projections are full, making the potential-response graph complete tripartite and every triple a maximal three-clique, including the deleted strict-middle valleys.  Their graph describes observable support implications, whereas \(Q_{3,L}\) also augments randomized marginals by the three unique-peak target coordinates.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer gives an exponential staircase facet family, exact catalogues for \(L\le5\), three-facet sharp endpoint formulas, exact polynomial-time scalar evaluation for rational inputs, sparse endpoint-attaining mixtures, a fixed-\(L\) plug-in rate, and finite-sample simultaneous endpoint honesty.  The open combinatorial layer asks for a finite renormalized predecessor classification and a literal \(\texttt{CHECK\_2BTAS}\)-accepted source whose soundness, completeness, and uniqueness hold for every \(L\).  Separately, regular-face Wald equivalence of the already honest exact scalar interval remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Russell (2021) studies sharp bounds for continuous functionals of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model through random-set restrictions and convex optimization.  Chiba (2017) studies the binary-treatment ordinal relative-treatment-effect parameter and gives exact randomization inference under independent potential outcomes.  Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive sharp cumulative formulas and attaining tables for unrestricted bivariate ordinal couplings.  Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive symbolic ordinal-benefit bounds for binary-exposure confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs.  None of these two-potential-outcome results transfers sharply to the present three-way forbidden support.  Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) give an arbitrary-objective multi-marginal transport architecture that can encode illegal cells by extended cost, but their quadratic-objective plug-in rate does not transfer to the indicator endpoint; the present legal-incidence linear program, exact separator, and rational polynomial-time computation are proved directly.  Finite linear-programming strong duality is used in the exact form of Trevisan (2011, Lecture 6, Theorem 6.5), while polynomial-time rational linear programming is drawn from Lecture 5, Section 2.4.  Kaido and Ponomarev (2025) characterize observable implications of support restrictions by compatibility graphs under a maximal-clique correspondence.  Every two-dose projection here is full, so the potential-response graph is complete tripartite and every triple is a maximal three-clique, including the strict-middle valleys deleted from \(\mathcal U_L\); consequently their requirement that every maximal clique correspond to a support point fails.  Their graph concerns observable support implications, whereas \(Q_{3,L}\) additionally carries the three unique-peak target coordinates.  Duarte et al. (2024) provide generic polynomial-program bounds, Bonet (2001) provides a causal-facet precedent, and Avis and Fukuda (1996) motivate duplicate-free predecessor enumeration, but none supplies the paper-specific finite predecessor map.  Cho and Russell (2024), Fang and Santos (2019), and Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) motivate perturbation and intersection-bound inference.  Here exact finite-sample simultaneous honesty and a fixed-\(L\) plug-in rate are proved; only regular-face Wald equivalence remains open.  Goodwin et al. (2022) provide the randomized three-dose setting, used solely for an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis under a prespecified score and an added, clinically unvalidated cross-world unimodality restriction.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The staircase family and the exact catalogues through \(L=5\) are proved, but they do not furnish the finite predecessor type set or an accepted all-\(L\) source.  In particular, the direct two-register encoding of alternating \(\mathrm L\) and \(\mathrm R\) staircase updates violates a fixed triangular order; a different representation within sixteen registers or an impossibility proof is still required.  Scalar endpoint formulas, polynomial-time rational computation, sparse attaining mixtures, fixed-\(L\) plug-in rates, and exact finite-sample simultaneous honesty do not depend on resolving that stream.  The only remaining inference issue is the uniform local normal and quantile approximation needed to prove regular-face Wald equivalence under the procedure's simultaneous error allocation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved results are the all-\(L\) staircase facet family, exact facet counts \(F_2=7\), \(F_3=59\), \(F_4=197\), and \(F_5=721\), sharp scalar endpoint formulas using at most three full facets, exact polynomial-time rational endpoint computation, endpoint-attaining rational mixtures with support at most \(3L-2\), the sharpness of that support bound at \(L=2\), the fixed-\(L\) plug-in rate, and exact finite-sample simultaneous endpoint honesty.  These endpoint and inference results are independent of the unresolved facet stream.  Open claims are confined to the existence or impossibility of one exact-once all-\(L\) two-pass stream with a finite predecessor and transfer classification, and to regular-face equivalence between the exact scalar interval and a semiparametrically efficient Wald interval with an explicitly matched critical value.  No scalar efficiency claim is made.  The Goodwin et al. use case is an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis based on the prespecified score: random assignment and consistency identify arm marginals, but the trial neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality, and no data analysis or empirical verification of that restriction is claimed.

statement_notes.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian's arbitrary-objective transport architecture can encode the support with extended costs, but its quadratic-objective rate does not transfer.  The present finite legal-support program and its exact algorithmic consequences are proved directly, using Trevisan's Theorem 6.5 for strong duality.
statement_notes.consumer: All six scalar endpoints and endpoint-attaining worst-case response mixtures can be computed before the all-\(L\) canonical joint-polytope stream is known.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(L\ge 2\), a compatible marginal vector \(p\), a dose \(d\in\mathcal D\), and either the lower- or upper-endpoint objective.  The first step is a finite-support elimination argument, proved directly here.  Index columns by \(u\in\mathcal U_L\), and let \(M\) be the \((3L-2)\)-by-\(|\mathcal U_L|\) matrix with one row indexed by \(\varnothing\) and the remaining rows indexed by \((r,j)\in\mathcal D\times\{1,\ldots,L-1\}\), where
\[
 M_{\varnothing,u}=1,
 \qquad
 M_{(r,j),u}=\mathbf 1\{u_r=j\}.
\]
Set
\[
 b(p)=\bigl(1,(p_{rj})_{r\in\mathcal D,\,1\le j<L}\bigr)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The definition \(\text{def:coupling-fiber}\) gives
\[
 \Gamma_L(p)=\{q\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal U_L}:Mq=b(p)\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, every \(q\in\Gamma_L(p)\) satisfies these equations.  Conversely, if \(q\ge0\) and \(Mq=b(p)\), then the first row gives \(\sum_u q(u)=1\), while for each \(r\in\mathcal D\) the omitted level-zero equation follows from
\[
 \sum_{u:u_r=0}q(u)
 =1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\sum_{u:u_r=j}q(u)
 =1-\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}p_{rj}
 =p_{r0}.
\]
The last equality uses the stated condition that each arm marginal \((p_{rj})_{j\in\mathcal Y_L}\) is a probability vector.  This proves (1).

Compatibility means that the set in (1) is nonempty.  It is closed and contained in the finite probability simplex, hence compact.  By \(\text{def:unique-peak-indicators}\),
\[
 q\longmapsto\theta_d(q)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}B_d(u)q(u)
\]
is linear and continuous, so it attains its minimum and maximum on \(\Gamma_L(p)\).

For either objective, choose an optimizer \(q^\star\) with minimum support, and put \(S=\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)\).  Suppose that the columns \((M_u)_{u\in S}\) were linearly dependent.  Then there would be a nonzero vector \(z\), supported on \(S\), with \(Mz=0\).  Since \(q^\star(u)>0\) for \(u\in S\), both \(q^\star+\varepsilon z\) and \(q^\star-\varepsilon z\) are nonnegative for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), and (1) makes both feasible.  For a minimum, both perturbed objective values are at least the optimum; for a maximum, both are at most the optimum.  Their average is the objective value at \(q^\star\), so in either case both are optimal and
\[
 \sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}B_d(u)z(u)=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
The mass row of \(Mz=0\) gives \(\sum_u z(u)=0\), so nonzero \(z\) has both signs.  Therefore
\[
 t=\min_{u\in S:z(u)<0}\frac{q^\star(u)}{-z(u)}>0
\]
makes \(q^\star+tz\) feasible, optimal by (2), and supported on a strict subset of \(S\), a contradiction.  Thus the columns indexed by \(S\) are linearly independent, and the explicit row count yields
\[
 |\operatorname{supp}(q^\star)|
 \le \operatorname{rank}(M)
 \le 3L-2.
 \tag{3}
\]

We next give the promised construction from an active facet certificate; this is a nonnegative-slack complementary-slackness argument.  For \(h_i\in\mathcal H_L\), write its inequality as
\[
 a_i(p)+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}\theta\ge0,
 \qquad
 a_i(p)=\kappa_i+
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal D}\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}\alpha_{irj}p_{rj}.
\]
For every \(q\in\Gamma_L(p)\), equations (1), the definition of \(\theta(q)\), and \(\text{def:canonical-facet-set}\) give the exact expectation identity
\[
 a_i(p)+\beta_i^{\mathsf T}\theta(q)
 =\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q(u)\ge0,
 \tag{4}
\]
because \(s_{h_i}(u)\ge0\) on the legal support \(\mathcal U_L\).

For a lower endpoint, \(\text{thm:sharp-three-facet-endpoints}\) supplies an attaining \(\lambda\in\mathcal D_d^-\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i=e_d,
 \qquad
 \underline\theta_d(p)=-\sum_i\lambda_i a_i(p),
 \qquad
 \lambda_i\ge0.
 \tag{5}
\]
Applying (4) to any lower-endpoint optimizer gives
\[
 0=\underline\theta_d(p)+\sum_i\lambda_i a_i(p)
 =\sum_i\lambda_i\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q^\star(u).
 \tag{6}
\]
All terms are nonnegative, so \(\lambda_i>0\) and \(q^\star(u)>0\) imply \(s_{h_i}(u)=0\).  For an upper endpoint, the same theorem supplies an attaining \(\mu\in\mathcal D_d^+\) with
\[
 \sum_i\mu_i\beta_i=-e_d,
 \qquad
 \overline\theta_d(p)=\sum_i\mu_i a_i(p),
 \qquad
 \mu_i\ge0,
 \tag{7}
\]
and (4) yields
\[
 0=\sum_i\mu_i a_i(p)-\overline\theta_d(p)
 =\sum_i\mu_i\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_L}s_{h_i}(u)q^\star(u).
 \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(\mu_i>0\) and \(q^\star(u)>0\) likewise imply \(s_{h_i}(u)=0\).

Let \(\rho\) denote the active certificate, either \(\lambda\) or \(\mu\), and define its common tight set by
\[
 T_\rho=\{u\in\mathcal U_L:s_{h_i}(u)=0
 \text{ for every }i\text{ with }\rho_i>0\}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Equations (6) and (8) show that
\[
 M_{T_\rho}q_{T_\rho}=b(p),
 \qquad q_{T_\rho}\ge0
 \tag{10}
\]
is nonempty.  Conversely, extend any solution of (10) by zero outside \(T_\rho\).  It belongs to \(\Gamma_L(p)\) by (1).  Summing (4) with the certificate weights gives equality in (5) or (7), so the extension attains the specified endpoint.  Applying the preceding support-elimination argument within (10) gives a solution supported on at most \(3L-2\) legal response types.

This also gives a finite exact construction.  Enumerate subsets \(S\subseteq T_\rho\) with \(|S|\le3L-2\), solve
\[
 M_Sq_S=b(p),\qquad q_S\ge0,
 \tag{11}
\]
and accept the first solution whose columns \(M_S\) are linearly independent.  Nonemptiness of (10) and the elimination proof guarantee success.  If \(p\) is rational, then \(b(p)\) is rational and all entries of \(M\) are integers.  Moreover, on the linearly independent support of an active certificate, the equations \(\sum_i\rho_i\beta_i=\pm e_d\) have a unique solution and a nonsingular integer minor, so the certificate weights are rational.  The tight set (9) is therefore exactly decidable using the integral slacks.  For an accepted support \(S\), choose \(|S|\) rows \(R\) for which the square integer matrix \(M_{R,S}\) is nonsingular.  Then
\[
 q_S=M_{R,S}^{-1}b_R(p)
\]
is rational; rational Gaussian elimination verifies the remaining equations and nonnegativity in (11).  Hence the active certificate and complementary slackness construct an endpoint-attaining mixture with rational masses.

Finally, the support cap in (3) is uniformly sharp in the sense required for an all-\(L\) guarantee.  Take \(L=2\) and \(p_{0,1}=p_{1,1}=p_{2,1}=1/2\).  By \(\text{def:non-valley-support}\), the only deleted binary triple is \(101\).  Write \(x_{abc}=q(a,b,c)\) for the seven legal triples.  The three level-one marginal equations are
\[
 x_{100}+x_{110}+x_{111}=\frac12,
 \quad
 x_{010}+x_{011}+x_{110}+x_{111}=\frac12,
 \quad
 x_{001}+x_{011}+x_{111}=\frac12.
 \tag{12}
\]
Combining (12) with \(\sum x_{abc}=1\) gives
\[
 x_{000}=x_{111}-x_{010}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Nonnegativity therefore implies \(x_{111}\ge x_{010}\).  By \(\text{def:unique-peak-indicators}\), \(B_1(u)=1\) only at \(u=010\), so \(\theta_1(q)=x_{010}\).  The middle equation in (12) and (13) yield
\[
 \frac12=x_{010}+x_{011}+x_{110}+x_{111}
 \ge2x_{010},
\]
and hence \(\overline\theta_1(p)\le1/4\).  The mixture
\[
 x_{001}=x_{010}=x_{100}=x_{111}=\frac14,
 \qquad
 x_{000}=x_{011}=x_{110}=0
 \tag{14}
\]
is supported on legal triples, satisfies all three marginals in (12), and has \(\theta_1=1/4\).  Thus \(\overline\theta_1(p)=1/4\).  If equality holds, then (12)--(13) force \(x_{111}=x_{010}=1/4\) and \(x_{011}=x_{110}=0\); the first and third equations in (12) then force \(x_{100}=x_{001}=1/4\), while (13) forces \(x_{000}=0\).  Therefore (14) is the unique optimizer, and every optimizer has support \(4=3L-2\).  In particular, the universal support guarantee cannot be reduced to \(3L-3\).  No division by an unknown probability, treatment-overlap argument, boundary limit, or asymptotic condition is used; the proof uses only finite \(L\), compatible arm-probability vectors, nonnegative masses on \(\mathcal U_L\), and the declared facet theorem.
